items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: I went up there as his musical director and arranger and saxophone player.

ctx.x: But Jimmy Dudley left and went to the Cotton Pickers. First he went to Billy Minor in Detroit and then he went to the Cotton Pickers. So anyway, we played around Milwaukee that winter and then we finally -- then I finally left there and we went to Minneapolis to play for the Stecker Brothers. And in that interim I had this -- I was playing from one band -- I played with Eli a while and then I'd play with Grant Moore a while, except for the time we got snowbound up there. And after switching from band to band and…

Then I had -- I was always itchy to go someplace so I wrote a fellow up in Toledo had a band called Frank Terry's Chicago Nightengales, I think it was. And I wrote them a letter and they sent for me and I went up there as his musical director and arranger and saxophone player. And this is where I met Art Tatum. Art Tatum was -- I was living on

City Park, right across the street from Art. And one night we played with the house band at the Recreation Ballroom there. And we would play five nights or six nights a week and on Monday we'd have off and we'd give a colored dance.
